- Input vs output pricing (we bill customers separately for user input and assistant output)
- Streaming vs non-streaming costs (if applicable)
- Any standard volume discounts or thresholds for hosted (1M / 10M / 100M tokens)
- Whether embeddings and reranking are priced differently

We’re just collecting numbers for a vendor short-list; a one-page rate card would be ideal. Can you get something over by EOD Tuesday PT?

Thanks — Lina

Hi Lina — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the clear ask — forwarding a compact baseline in-line below and attaching the Q2 rate card and a short model note. Marissa (Sales Engineering) and Ben (Account Exec) are looped for follow up and any pricing discussion.

Summary (Hosted API, per 1M tokens):
- Standard (base) tier: Input: $0.80 / 1M tokens | Output: $1.60 / 1M tokens
- Latency-optimized: Input: $1.25 / 1M tokens | Output: $2.50 / 1M tokens
- Cost-optimized (quantized variants): Input: $0.35 / 1M tokens | Output: $0.70 / 1M tokens

Notes:
- Streaming output billing is the same token-level counting as non-streaming; no separate streaming surcharge.
- Embeddings: flat $0.004 per 1k tokens equivalent (or $4.00 per 1M input-token-equivalents) — typically priced separately from generation IO.
- Reranking / small-batch model endpoints often use the cost-optimized rates above; we can recommend a specific model depending on latency requirements.

Volume guidance (hosted API):
- 0–1M tokens / mo: base tier rates
- 1M–10M tokens / mo: 5% off base list with a 3-mo prepay or card on file
- 10M–100M tokens / mo: 12–18% off with a 6–12 mo committed plan (negotiable by use case)
- 100M+ tokens / mo: custom committed pricing and dedicated support (refer to Dedicated product)

Model catalog (hosted highlights, short commentary):
- redwood-legacy-1.0 (cost-optimized): good for high-throughput batch; lower RAM footprint; recommended for bulk background tasks.
- redwood-std-2.1 (balanced): default choice for chat-like UX; balanced latency/cost.
- redwood-latency-1 (latency-optimized): lower p99 latency for real-time experiences; higher per-token cost.
- open-compat-gptx (compatibility tier): lower cost for cross-vendor model switch; slightly slower for long contexts.

Attachments included: Redwood_Baseline_Ratecard_Q2_2026.pdf (summary table + notes), HealthCo_Rate_Request_Answers.xlsx (pro forma answers we filled out).

Next steps: If you can share a rough monthly token forecast (expected monthly user messages and average output length), Marissa can put together a simple projection and a sample discount scenario. We can also schedule a 30-min call Tues/Wed to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,

Hey Lina — Marissa here. Quick answers inline and a projection at the bottom.

1) Quantization & quality: our cost-optimized tier typically uses 8-bit quantization (dynamic per-kernel). For many instruction-following tasks the quality delta vs standard is minimal; for safety-sensitive clinical language we recommend A/B evals on a small prompt set. If you want, we’ll run 100 prompt evals free of charge.

2) Streaming token counting: we count generated tokens as they are emitted. Intermediate partial chunks are counted the same as final tokens; in short, billing is per generated token regardless of chunking. No double-billing for re-sent partials.

4M token projection (monthly) — using Base tier with a 12% committed discount (6-mo):
- Input tokens (assume 1:1 user input to generated output for your flows): 2M input tokens @ base $0.80 = $1,600 -> after 12% = $1,408
- Output tokens: 2M output tokens @ base $1.60 = $3,200 -> after 12% = $2,816
- Total monthly (generation IO): $4,224
- Embeddings (if used for similarity search): estimated 0.5M embedding-token-equivalents @ $4.00 per 1M = $2.00/mo (negligible at pilot scale)

We’ve attached a simple spreadsheet (HealthCo_Rate_Request_Answers.xlsx) with line items and a link to a HubSpot quote draft: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HC-2026-07-01 (you can view the draft if you share emails).

If the numbers look OK, Ben can draft a short pilot SOW and outline payment terms. Would 6 months with a monthly invoice work or do you prefer an upfront invoice?

Thanks — happy to run the evals you need.
